title: Robustness fixes from the parser & IO review
summary:
Fixes the defects found by the 2026-10-12 review of argument parsing, child-process handling, external-output parsing and silent-failure defaults (finding numbers refer to that review). Most of them failed silently, like the `ff plan --bg` bug that dropped the feature text.

Out of scope: per-stage tool access (separate epic), npm .cmd shim support, bare-repo/submodule support, and remaining low-severity edge cases not named in a ticket.

tickets.title: Harden child-process execution
tickets.goal: A child process that fails early, emits multi-byte text, waits for stdin or hangs is reported accurately instead of crashing ff, garbling output or blocking for 30 minutes.
inScope: lib/exec.mjs run(): handle stdin 'error' (finding 7) so an early child exit rejects normally with exit code and stderr
decode stdout/stderr as UTF-8 streams in run() and runShell() (finding 8)
runShell(): stdin closed/ignored (finding 9)
runShell() timeout on Windows kills the whole process tree and reports the timeout explicitly (finding 10)
error message puts stderr before the (truncated) argument list (finding 12)
dod: run() with a child that exits immediately while 5 MB of stdin is being written rejects (or resolves with allowFail) with the exit code; the ff process does not crash
a child that writes a multi-byte character split across two chunks is read back exactly
runShell() of a command that waits for stdin EOF returns promptly
runShell() of a command that outlives timeoutMs returns within about 2 s of the timeout, with a result marked as timed out, and leaves no child process running
the error message of a failed run() contains the child's stderr even when the argument list is several KB long
tests: timeout kills the tree and is flagged
qaHints: Run ff doctor and an ff run on the sandbox to confirm nothing regressed

tickets.title: Only a genuine failing test counts as a verified red phase
tickets.goal: The red phase is verified only when the test run actually reports failing tests, not when the runner crashed, timed out or was not found.
inScope: lib/run.mjs red gate and lib/stages.mjs red prompt/schema (finding 11)
red result reports the names of the failing tests it wrote; ff checks the test output shows failures and those names
timeouts and runner errors (exit code null, command not found) are rejected as red evidence with a clear history message for the next attempt
outOfScope: parsing every test runner's output format; a name match plus a non-null nonzero exit is enough
dod: a red gate whose test run timed out is not committed as test: and is recorded as a failed red phase
a red gate whose output does not mention any of the reported failing test names is not committed
a red gate with a nonzero exit and the reported test names in its output is committed as before
the red_failed event records the reason
qaHints: On the sandbox, a normal ff run still produces test: then feat: commits

tickets.title: Worktrees survive title edits and leftovers
tickets.goal: Re-running a ticket works after its title changed or a stale folder was left behind, and cleanup never deletes unsaved work.
inScope: branch for an existing ticket worktree is read from the worktree, not re-derived from the current title (finding 16)
an existing path is reused only if it is a git worktree of this repo on a ticket branch; otherwise ff stops with a clear error (finding 17)
cleanupMerged skips worktrees with uncommitted changes or unpushed commits and logs why (finding 18)
dod: a ticket whose title changed after its worktree was created pushes to the existing branch
a plain directory at the worktree path makes ff run fail that ticket with a message naming the path
cleanupMerged leaves a merged ticket's worktree in place when it has uncommitted changes
qaHints: Rename a sandbox ticket mid-flight and re-run ff run

tickets.title: Publishing never silently drops or duplicates tickets
tickets.goal: ff publish rejects malformed plans up front and, if GitHub fails mid-way, reports exactly what was created.
inScope: duplicate ticket keys and a missing or empty tickets array are rejected before any issue is created (finding 21)
a failure part-way through publishing reports the epic and ticket numbers already created (finding 22)
plan and eval JSON files are read BOM-tolerantly and parse errors name the file (finding 25)
createIssue fails clearly if gh does not return an issue URL instead of passing NaN on (finding 14)
dod: publishing a plan with two tickets sharing a key throws before creating anything
a simulated failure on the third issue throws an error that lists the epic and the two created ticket numbers
a plan file saved with a UTF-8 BOM publishes; an invalid one errors with its file name
an unexpected gh output for issue creation throws instead of returning NaN
qaHints: Publish eval/plan.json in the sandbox after saving it with a BOM

tickets.title: Config and commands parse without silent losses
tickets.goal: Repo overrides and AGENTS.md commands behave as written: nested overrides keep sibling settings and hyphenated or duplicate command names are not silently lost.
inScope: mergeConfig deep-merges plain objects at every level; arrays and scalars replace (finding 24)
__proto__, constructor and prototype keys are ignored when merging
## Commands accepts hyphenated names such as lint-js; duplicate names produce a warning (finding 23)
README documents the merge rule
dod: overriding toolkit.claude.plugins keeps toolkit.claude.hooks from the lower layer
overriding contextBudget.byModel.opus keeps the other byModel entries
- lint-js: `x` is parsed as lint-js
two test: lines produce a warning naming the duplicate
qaHints: ff config in the sandbox shows unchanged defaults

tickets.title: No silent no-ops or stuck tickets
tickets.goal: A run that has nothing to do, fails to update GitHub or leaves tickets stuck says so and exits non-zero, and stuck tickets can be recovered.
inScope: a failed needs-human / in-progress label update is logged and recorded as an event instead of swallowed (finding 29)
ff run detects tickets labelled in-progress with no live ff run (lock file with pid per epic) and reports them; --retry-stuck clears the label so they run again (finding 29)
an epic with zero sub-issues, or with nothing ready, explains why and exits non-zero (finding 30)
ff stats --refresh counts and reports PRs it could not refresh (finding 31)
diff stats failure is logged rather than recorded as zeros (finding 32)
outOfScope: automatic retry of stuck tickets without the flag
dod: a label update failure appears in the run log and events with the ticket number
an in-progress ticket from a dead run is reported by ff run, and ff run --retry-stuck runs it
ff run on an issue with no sub-issues exits non-zero with an explanation
ff stats --refresh prints how many PRs failed to refresh
qaHints: Kill an ff run mid-ticket in the sandbox, then run again with --retry-stuck

tickets.title: Strict, validated CLI options
tickets.goal: Typos, missing values and bad numbers in ff commands produce a clear error and usage instead of silently doing something else.
inScope: per-command allowlists of value and boolean flags; unknown flags are rejected (finding 1)
--flag=value form (finding 2)
a value flag with no value is an error (finding 3)
-- ends option parsing (finding 4)
dispatch uses own properties only (finding 5)
ff --help and ff <command> --help print usage and exit 0; epic numbers and --runs must be positive integers (findings 6, 34)
dod: ff plan --bgg "x" fails with an unknown-flag error
ff eval --runs=3 a.json runs 3 times
ff eval --plan with no value fails with usage
ff plan --bg -- "--weird" passes --weird as the feature text
ff constructor prints usage and exits 1
ff run abc and ff eval --runs three fail with a clear error
qaHints: Try a few typo'd commands and check the messages
